defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Review 1: Eager removal of new_m not rolled back when old_m not found (scene loses new_m)
Review 1: new_m removed from wrong nesting level when old_m found deeper
Review 1: Replacing an object with itself now raises ValueError
Review 1 (nit): Should search first, then remove new_m from same list
Review 1: Tests don't cover failed replace, same-object replace, or cross-level cases
Review 2: Removal runs before search, not rolled back on failure
Review 2: new_m removed at wrong nesting level on recursive descent
Review 2: Replacing an object with itself now raises ValueError
Review 2: list.remove only drops first match, leaving duplicates
Review 2 (nit): Guard uses == instead of is
Review 2 (nit): Removal should happen after search succeeds, at replacement site
Review 2: Tests don't cover the failure modes
votes.evidence_quote: When `old_m` and `new_m` are the same object, line 38 removes it from the list before the search runs; the search then cannot find it and raises on line 52.
votes.justification: The review explicitly flags that scene.replace(square, square) now raises ValueError. It traces this to the dedup removal at the top of replace_in_list running before the search, which is the known defect. Separately, it notes that the eager removal is not rolled back on failure, so the object is left removed.
